title: Predicate type: SLSA Provenance - in-toto/attestation
snippet: The in-toto Attestation Framework defines a fixed, lightweight Statement that communicates information about software supply chain execution through a Predicate using context-specific schema identified by a Predicate Type, applying to one or more software supply chain Subjects.
claim: in-toto attestations have fixed lightweight Statement structure with predicates and subjects for supply chain attestation

query: in-toto attestation framework DSSE SLSA v1.0 provenance 2026
title: DSSE - Dead Simple Signing Envelope
snippet: An in-toto attestation has two layers: the DSSE envelope and the statement. DSSE is a lightweight container format for signed payloads standardized at secure-systems-lab. DSSE provides signature verification without embedding public keys in the attestation, enabling portable verification by external tools.
claim: DSSE provides lightweight signed envelope structure for portable attestation verification without embedded keys

query: in-toto attestation framework DSSE SLSA v1.0 provenance 2026
title: SLSA • Provenance
snippet: SLSA Provenance v1.0 is a predicate type within the in-toto framework. When a SLSA-compliant build platform generates provenance, it produces an in-toto attestation with predicateType: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1, signs it with DSSE, and associates it with the built artifact via the subject field. Provenance captures builder identity, build instructions, parameters, environment variables, and dependency digests.
claim: SLSA v1.0 provenance is official predicate type for build artifacts; standard version is v1.0

topic: Sigstore keyless signing with transparency log
query: Sigstore keyless signing transparency log verification
title: Overview - Sigstore
snippet: Sigstore provides keyless signing through ephemeral key signing where users verify artifacts using a transparency log for signature verification rather than keys. Sigstore's keyless methods include Fulcio (certificate authority for short-lived signing certificates issued based on OpenID Connect identity) and Rekor (transparency log recording every signature in a non-modifiable way).
claim: Sigstore enables keyless signing using Fulcio (ephemeral certs from OIDC) and Rekor (public transparency log) for verification

query: supply chain security attestation artifact verification standards
title: Attestation: Definition, Explanation & Role in SLSA Compliance & Supply Chain Integrity
snippet: Attestation in software supply chain security is a digitally signed document making claims about software artifacts, their origins, processes used to create them, and security measures applied during lifecycle. Supply chain attestation connects a trusted build to a running workload through cryptographic signatures and provenance records. Verification is performed automatically by tools against verifiable metadata.
claim: Attestation is cryptographically signed claim about artifacts; verification by external tools is essential requirement

topic: RFC 9162 Certificate Transparency for append-only logs
query: in-toto attestation framework DSSE SLSA v1.0 provenance 2026
title: RFC 9162 - Certificate Transparency Version 2.0
snippet: RFC 9162 defines an append-only Merkle log with inclusion and consistency proofs. RFC 8785 defines JSON Canonicalization Scheme for canonical byte form to hash. Together they provide the integrity primitives for append-only state stores, enabling attestations to be chained to a log head with external verification.
claim: RFC 9162 defines Merkle log structure with proofs; RFC 8785 defines canonical bytes; standards enable verifiable log chains

query: in-toto attestation framework DSSE SLSA v1.0 provenance 2026
title: in-toto Attestation Framework v1
snippet: The in-toto Attestation Framework v1 is published and stable. DSSE is the signed envelope format for attestations. The framework is designed for interoperability: attestations produced by one tool can be verified by another tool, without shared infrastructure or vendor lock-in.
claim: in-toto Attestation Framework v1 is published standard enabling cross-tool attestation verification
